title: Lockstep Run Under Output Capture
statement: Let $M$ be a Boolean Turing machine with $k$ work tapes and states $S$, and let $N$ be a Boolean Turing machine with $k+1$ work tapes and states $H$. Fix a map $emb:S\to H$, a state $ret\in H$, and suppose that for every state $s\in S$, input symbol $inp$ (possibly absent), and assignment $w$ of symbols to the $k+1$ work-tape heads, the transition of $N$ at $(emb(s),inp,w)$ is the capture transform of the transition of $M$ at $(s,inp,w|_{k})$, using the first $k$ entries of $w$. For every Boolean input word, prefix word $pre$, output word $out_0$, initial configuration $c_0$ of $M$, and $t\in\mathbb N$, if $M$ is not halted at any time $t'<t$ when run from $c_0$, then running $N$ for $t$ steps from the capture image of $c_0$ equals the capture image of the configuration reached by running $M$ for $t$ steps from $c_0$.
hypotheses_covered: A Boolean Turing machine $M$ with $k$ work tapes and state set $S$
A Boolean Turing machine $N$ with $k+1$ work tapes and state set $H$
The transition-agreement hypothesis for all $s$, optional input symbols, and $k+1$-tape head-symbol assignments
Prefix word $pre$ and initial output word $out_0$
Nonhalting of $M$ at every time $t'<t$ from $c_0$
replaced:
Let $M$ be a Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet with $k$ work tapes and state set
$S$, let $N$ be one with $k+1$ work tapes and state set $H$, and let $\iota : S \to H$
and $r \in H$. Suppose that for every $s \in S$, every (possibly blank) input symbol
$\sigma$ and every tuple $(w_0, \dots, w_k)$ of work-tape symbols, the transition of $N$
at $(\iota(s), \sigma, w_0, \dots, w_k)$ is the capture transform of the transition of
$M$ at $(s, \sigma, w_0, \dots, w_{k-1})$: $M$'s action on the input and first $k$ tapes,
its emitted bit (if any) written on the last tape followed by a right move, no output,
and a halt replaced by entering $r$. Let $p$, $o$ be Boolean words, $c_0$ a
configuration of $M$ on an input $x$, and $t \in \mathbb{N}$ such that $M$ run from $c_0$
is not halted at any time $t' < t$; then running $N$ for $t$ steps from the capture image
of $c_0$ yields the capture image of the configuration $M$ reaches after $t$ steps from
$c_0$, where the capture image of a configuration $c$ has state $\iota(q)$ (or $r$ if $c$
is halted), the input head and work tapes of $c$ on the first $k$ tapes, the word $p$
followed by the output of $c$ stored from cell $0$ of the last tape with that head just
past its end, and output $o$.
